findings.title: Novelty (TM-score to nearest PDB) column of Table 3 has no computing code
findings.quote:
FoldSeek (van Kempen et al., 2022) to report diversity as
the number of unique clusters while novelty is the average
TM-score (Zhang & Skolnick, 2005) of each sample to its
most similar protein in PDB.
findings.claim: Table 3 reports a Novelty (NOV.) value for every method (e.g. Multiflow 0.61), defined as the average TM-score of each generated sample to its most similar protein in the PDB. No function in the multiflow package computes a TM-score to a PDB reference set — FoldSeek is invoked only for easy-cluster diversity (experiments/utils.py:75-104), and the only other TM machinery is openfold's predicted-TM confidence head. A whole-package grep returns 0 hits (_audit_code/out/missing_metrics.txt).
findings.concern: The Novelty column of the headline co-design table cannot be reproduced from the repository; the number that supports 'comparable ... novelty to previous approaches' is not traceable to any script.
findings.resolution: Authors: please provide the novelty script (e.g. FoldSeek/TMalign search of each designable sample against the PDB and averaging the top TM-score), including the reference PDB set used.

findings.title: Section 6.1 text8 experiment (Table 5, Figure 2) has no code in the repo
findings.quote: Table 5. Model log-likelihoods computed on the test set of text8 in bits-per-character (BPC).
findings.claim: Section 6.1, Table 5, and Figure 2 present the DFM text-modeling results (character-level 86M-parameter transformer on text8, D3PM / SEDD / autoregressive baselines, GPT-J-6B NLL and entropy, and BPC log-likelihood bounds via Eq. 24). The audited repository contains only the protein (Multiflow) codebase; a whole-package grep for text8 / BPC / GPT-J / D3PM / SEDD / autoregressive / character-level returns 0 hits (_audit_code/out/missing_metrics.txt).
findings.concern: The empirical evidence for the DFM-vs-diffusion claim (that DFMs improve over D3PM/SEDD) — an entire experimental section, one table, and one figure — cannot be reproduced from this repository.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether the text8 code lives in the separately-cited discrete_flow_models repo (README references it) and, if so, link the exact scripts that produce Table 5 and Figure 2; otherwise release that code.

findings.title: No code computes the ± std / standard errors reported in Tables 4, 6 and Figure 3
findings.quote:
'Total designable': top_sample_csv.designable.sum(),
'Designable': top_sample_csv.designable.mean(),
'Total samples': len(top_sample_csv),
'Average_bb_rmsd': top_sample_csv.bb_rmsd.mean(),
'Average_seq_recovery': top_sample_csv.inv_fold_seq_recovery.mean(),
'Average_pmpnn_bb_rmsd': top_sample_csv.pmpnn_bb_rmsd.mean(),
'Average_pmpnn_seq_recovery': top_sample_csv.pmpnn_seq_recovery.mean(),
findings.claim: The metric functions compute only means (.mean()); no .std() / SEM / multi-seed aggregation exists anywhere in the multiflow package (grep for .std(/.sem/standard error returns only unrelated subprocess `stderr=` and a weight-init `truncnorm.std`). Yet Table 4 is captioned 'mean ± std', Table 6 gives Table 3 'with standard error', Figure 3 error bars are 'the standard error', and §6.2.1 reports 'the average of three seeds'.
findings.concern: The dispersion figures (± std, standard errors, error bars) and the three-seed averaging cannot be reproduced from the repo; only point-estimate means are produced by the shipped code.
findings.resolution: Authors: provide the aggregation script that averages the three seeds and computes the standard deviations / standard errors shown in Table 4, Table 6 and Figure 3 (the per-sample values are saved to the CSVs, so this is recoverable).
findings.paper_ref: Table 4 caption ('mean ± std'); Table 6; Figure 3 ('Error bars show the standard error'); §6.2.1 ('average of three seeds')

findings.title: Diversity is the raw FoldSeek cluster count, unnormalized by number of designable samples
findings.claim: Diversity (Table 3 DIV.) is the number of FoldSeek structural clusters among the designable samples: calculate_diversity clusters only designable_samples, and run_easy_cluster returns len(rep_seq_fasta) i.e. the raw cluster count (experiments/utils.py:104). It is not divided by the number of designable samples.
findings.concern: A raw cluster count scales with how many samples are designable, so a method with higher designability can register higher 'diversity' for reasons unrelated to structural variety, partly confounding the cross-method comparison in Table 3.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm the raw cluster count is intended (it is the field convention used by RFdiffusion/FrameFlow); optionally also report clusters normalized by the number of designable samples so the comparison controls for designability.
